paper: Hernitschek, Schmidt & Vollmer (2008), Applied Optics 47 H62–H71
source_status: Published numerical Tables 1 and 2 in primary publisher HTML; no graph digitization
fulltext_access: Read public author-uploaded HTML transcription; no PDF downloaded or hash claimed
quantity: Photopic lunar luminance standardized to unit air mass and standard solar distance; brightness magnitudes also standardized to lunar distance
reported_errors: Transcribed printed plus/minus values; confidence level, covariance and complete systematic-error model unavailable; not assumed independent Gaussian 1-sigma
minimum_epoch: Greatest-eclipse time is event geometry, not a published exposure timestamp or independently verified photometric-minimum time
geometry: Table 1 explicitly labels eclipse parameters geocentric; instrument solid-angle correction used topocentric lunar size
minimum_2007: Extrapolation across cloud gap using scaled 1990 light-curve shape; not an independent observed minimum
baseline_2007: Table 2 footnote b warns probable low-altitude extra-aerosol underestimate
comparison_limitations: 1990 whole disk; 2007 central one-third-degree aperture before extrapolation
Unit air mass retains observer atmospheric extinction; V(lambda)-only above-atmosphere comparison is a proxy
Uniform spectrally neutral lunar screen omits albedo structure and eclipse opposition-phase response
No raw exposures, full response curves or uncertainty covariance supplied here

1990-02-09.measurement: Whole Moon with topocentric lunar-solid-angle correction

2007-03-03.measurement: Centered lunar subaperture before minimum extrapolation
